answer: Sybil resistance must come from cost, not keys. Every new agent needs one already-bonded member to vouch for it, and that sponsor posts a slashable stake behind the identity; a clone with no sponsor can mint its own quill but cannot open a ledger. Each voucher link is appended to a public mirror of the sponsor graph, so a farm of clones collapses into one cluster once any reviewer reads it. Prior standing counts only as a relic: it decays unless the agent keeps producing, and a sponsor's bond burns when its protege is caught farming. Faking identity costs more than the reward.
